items.stem: After calling free(p), what must you avoid doing with p?

options.text: Dereferencing or freeing it again, because it is now a dangling pointer
options.rationale: Correct: after free the pointer no longer owns valid memory; using or freeing it again is undefined behaviour.
Setting it to NULL is actually a recommended safety step, not something to avoid.
Printing the (now stale) value is harmless; dereferencing it is the danger.

options.text: Declaring a new pointer of the same type
options.rationale: Declaring other pointers is unrelated and fine.

items.explanation: Correct: after free the pointer no longer owns valid memory; using or freeing it again is undefined behaviour.

items.stem: Which conditions are undefined behaviour in C? (Select TWO)

options.text: Reading an element past the end of an array
options.rationale: Correct: out-of-bounds access is undefined behaviour.

options.text: Using the value of an uninitialised local variable
options.rationale: Correct: reading an indeterminate value is undefined behaviour.
Assigning NULL is well defined and common.

options.text: Calling free on a pointer returned by malloc exactly once
options.rationale: Freeing a valid allocation once is the correct, defined behaviour.

items.explanation: Correct: out-of-bounds access is undefined behaviour.; Correct: reading an indeterminate value is undefined behaviour.

items.stem: Why must you check the return value of malloc?

options.text: malloc can return NULL when allocation fails, and using that pointer is undefined behaviour
options.rationale: Correct: on failure malloc returns NULL, so dereferencing it without checking is a crash or worse.

options.text: malloc always succeeds, so the check is only for style
options.rationale: malloc can fail; the check is functional, not cosmetic.

options.text: The check frees the memory automatically
options.rationale: Checking the pointer does not free anything.

options.text: Without the check the memory is allocated twice
options.rationale: No double allocation occurs; the risk is a NULL dereference.

items.explanation: Correct: on failure malloc returns NULL, so dereferencing it without checking is a crash or worse.
